title: Backlit subjects
summary: Subject against bright sky or water: the meter sees the glow and drops your subject into silhouette.
why: The bright background dominates the average, so the camera underexposes the one thing you care about. You choose: expose the subject (sky blows) or keep the silhouette (subject goes black). Both are pictures — pick on purpose.

steps.text: Or: spot metering + focus point on the subject's face
Check the blinkies — background should clip, subject shouldn't

pitfalls: For a deliberate silhouette, do the opposite: −1.0 EV and expose for the sky.
levelUp: Backlight is rim light: a hair's-width of glow around hair, horse manes, and grass. Slight underexposure of the subject keeps the rim burning.
